To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) CCGs can be induced with a simple algorithm, b) the induced grammars perform as well as or even better than other systems when tested on longer sentences, and c) this performance is due to the expressive power of CCGs, and the fact that they can be induced without any prior linguistic knowledge.

(1) a simple unsupervised grammar induction algorithm for CCGs, (2) with a minimal number of general linguistic principles, (3) and with no prior language specific information, (4) can be used to learn grammars that (5) are robust to longer sentences and (6) achieve state of the art results on the WSJ corpus.

(1) unsupervised grammar induction is possible for Combinatory Grammars; (2) the grammar can remain robust when parsing longer and longer sentences; (3) this can be accomplished with a simple EM based algorithm, without prior language specific knowledge.
